name: Waking Before the Ruin
summary: A life ends — on a scaffold, at the hands of a sworn brother, in a bed of regrets — and consciousness resumes in a body with a boy's hands, under a ceiling from before the fire, beside a calendar three years wrong. Disbelief gives way to checking: the date, a face not yet aged, a scar that has not happened. Out of that checking comes the vow that this time the ending already lived through will not be allowed to arrive.

roles.label: the one who wakes earlier
constraints: carries a complete memory of what came after

roles.label: the fact that proves the date

beats.label: The life ends
beats.intent: the prior life closes on a defined loss or betrayal

beats.label: Waking earlier

examples.text: The ceiling was the one from before the fire, and the calendar on the wall was three years wrong, and his hands were a boy's hands.

name: Positioned Before It Happens
summary: A remembered event still sits in the future — the flood that takes the low fields, the house that calls in its loans, the question that will be on the examination, the caravan that arrives in spring — so a position is taken months early that looks like ruin to everyone watching: buying worthless land, refusing a good match, selling at the top of a rising market. The event arrives on schedule, the position pays, and the profit is inseparable from the question of how it could have been known.

roles.label: those who think it reckless
constraints: are reasoning correctly from what they know

beats.label: The event is remembered
beats.intent: a dated future event is recalled with usable precision

beats.label: The position is taken early
beats.intent: a commitment is made that looks reckless to every observer

beats.label: The event arrives on time
beats.intent: the remembered event happens exactly as expected

beats.label: Profit and suspicion together
beats.intent: the gain is banked and the question of how it was known is planted

preconditions.text: a remembered future event with a date and a usable consequence

effects.text: material or political advantage is secured ahead of everyone else
at least one observer now wonders how it could have been known

examples.text: He bought the flooded fields at the price of dry ones, and endured the laughter for eleven months, and then it rained.

name: The Memory Stops Matching
summary: An early intervention works, and its consequences spread past the thing it was meant to change: people who should have died marry, a house that should have fallen holds, a war starts a season late. One by one the remembered dates stop delivering, until the advantage that made the protagonist untouchable has quietly expired and they are walking into a future as unknown to them as it is to everyone else — having spent the last of the map.

roles.label: the one losing the map
constraints: built their plans on the remembered script

roles.label: the remembered future
constraints: degrades in proportion to their own success

roles.label: those whose lives already diverged
constraints: now act in ways the memory cannot predict

beats.label: The ripple spreads

effects.text: foreknowledge is no longer reliable and cannot be restored

examples.text: The grain riot she had been positioned for since spring simply never came, and she stood in the market understanding that from here she was as blind as everyone else in it.

name: The Traitor Everyone Still Trusts
summary: The one who will hand them over is standing in the courtyard pouring the wine, well-liked and guilty of precisely nothing yet, and there is no accusation that would not sound like madness or malice. So the counter is built sideways and unexplained — a seal moved to a different cupboard, a document quietly copied, a junior officer cultivated — until the betrayal arrives on the day it always arrived and lands on a floor that was prepared for it.

roles.label: the one who knows
constraints: cannot accuse without proof of a future act

roles.label: those who trust them
constraints: would side with the traitor today

beats.label: Recognising the face
beats.intent: the future betrayer is encountered before any offence exists

beats.label: Accusation is impossible
beats.intent: any warning would read as madness or malice

beats.label: Counter-positioning in silence
beats.intent: the ground is quietly prepared without naming the reason

beats.label: The betrayal lands on prepared ground
beats.intent: the treachery happens on schedule and fails

effects.text: the remembered sequence has been altered at a dated point: the betrayal came and failed

examples.text: He poured the wine himself, smiling, and she thanked him for it, and made a note of which cupboard the seal was kept in.

name: The Date That Is Coming
summary: Someone who was buried is alive again by virtue of the return, sitting at the table and complaining about the rice, with the date of their death coming up on the calendar and nothing yet changed. Everything is spent to break the sequence — the road avoided, the physician fetched early, the letter intercepted — and it works, and the price is taken from somewhere nobody thought to guard, because a death prevented is not a death cancelled.

roles.label: the one intercepting
constraints: knows the date and the manner

roles.label: where the cost lands instead
constraints: was not defended because it was not foreseen

beats.intent: the lost person is present and ordinary

beats.label: The date approaches
beats.intent: the remembered day comes closer with nothing yet changed

beats.label: The interception
beats.intent: everything is spent to break the sequence

beats.label: The cost lands elsewhere
beats.intent: the price is paid somewhere undefended

preconditions.text: a specific remembered death with a known date and manner

effects.text: the remembered sequence has been altered at a dated point: the person is alive past the date they should not have passed

examples.text: She kept him off the river road on the ninth, and it worked, and it was the boy who had run to warn him that they buried instead.

name: Knowledge From Somewhere Else
summary: A remedy, a way of boiling water, a method of reckoning accounts, a trick of casting or grafting from another world or another century is used where nobody here could have derived it, and it plainly works in front of witnesses. The result must then be given a cause this world can hold — a prodigy, a god's favour, a lost lineage, heresy — and whichever explanation the world settles on becomes a role that has to be performed from then on.

roles.label: the one who knows impossibly
constraints: cannot cite a source that exists here

roles.label: those who saw it work
constraints: must fit it into their own world-model

beats.label: Applied where it cannot come from
beats.intent: knowledge with no local origin is used openly

beats.label: It plainly works
beats.intent: the result is undeniable in front of witnesses

beats.label: An explanation is chosen
beats.intent: the world assigns a cause it can accept

beats.label: The explanation binds
beats.intent: the accepted attribution becomes a role that must be maintained

preconditions.text: a setting whose knowledge base plainly excludes what is being used

effects.text: the protagonist now occupies a role assigned by others
the true source of the knowledge is a secret with consequences

examples.text: He boiled the water and the ward stopped dying, and by the second week they had decided he was touched by a god, which was easier for everyone.

name: Answering for a Life Not Lived
summary: The body arrives with its own history attached: creditors at the gate with a note in handwriting that matches theirs, a betrothal agreed to by someone else, enemies made over years they did not live, a reputation already in circulation. The truth is unsayable, so the debts have to be paid, repudiated or grown into — and the manner of answering is what turns a borrowed life into their own.

roles.label: the one now wearing the life
those owed by the previous occupant

beats.label: The claims arrive
beats.intent: obligations and enmities of the previous life present themselves

beats.label: The truth cannot be told
beats.intent: the real explanation would be worse than the accusation

beats.label: The debts are answered
beats.intent: the newcomer pays, refuses, or renegotiates in their own manner

beats.label: Written into the life
beats.intent: the manner of answering makes the borrowed life genuinely theirs

preconditions.text: an occupied body and identity whose pre-existing obligations are not the protagonist's, with witnesses to them

effects.text: the inherited obligations are resolved on the newcomer's own terms
the newcomer is now the author of this life rather than its tenant

examples.text: Three men came for a debt she had never borrowed, and she found she could either deny a signature in her own hand or pay it.

name: The Slip That Cannot Be Explained
summary: A reflex gives it away — reaching for a latch in a room never entered, flinching at a name not yet spoken here, a word from a language this province has never heard — and one person sees it. They do not accuse. They simply begin watching, and every ordinary evening afterwards wears the cover story thinner, until the choice is between a lie that has to keep growing and confiding in someone whose reaction cannot be predicted.

beats.label: A reflex betrays it
beats.intent: an impossible familiarity shows before it can be masked

beats.label: Someone notices and says nothing

beats.label: The cover thins

beats.label: Deepen the lie or confide
beats.intent: the protagonist must commit to concealment or to a person

preconditions.text: a protagonist maintaining a false account of who they are

effects.text: one other party holds a suspicion that is essentially correct
the protagonist has either an accomplice or a watcher

examples.text: She reached for the latch on the left before anyone had shown her the room, and the old servant's eyes did not leave her for the rest of the evening.
